bodies.intuition: A model being trained takes far more memory than the same model being used. Adam keeps two extra numbers per parameter, and a full-precision master copy adds a third — so the weights are often less than a third of what training actually holds.
bodies.engineer: For Adam in mixed precision the standard accounting is 16 bytes per parameter: 4 for the fp32 master weight, 4 and 4 for the two moments, 4 for the fp32 gradient. That is why a model that infers comfortably on one accelerator needs several to train, and why sharding the state was the first thing distributed training attacked.
bodies.math: Per parameter: 2 bytes bf16 weight + 4 master + 4 momentum + 4 variance + 4 gradient ≈ 18. A 7B model therefore needs roughly 120 GB of state before activations, against 14 GB to serve it in bf16.
